quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #17
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator sticks while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks while driving, keep your eyes on the road. Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly. Then pull off the road safely and turn off the engine.

questions.question: At a school crossing sign, you should:

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross first. Watch carefully for pedestrians when driving through intersections or turning.

questions.question: If you need to drive in foggy weather:

options.text: Turn on your low beam headlights.
Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Do not drive faster than 10 miles per hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must use your headlights when you cannot see clearly. Use low beams in fog or rain. High beams reflect light back at you and make it harder to see.

questions.question: As you near an intersection, the traffic light turns yellow. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Be prepared to stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on an interstate highway:

options.text: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
Roll down your window and ask another driver for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.
questions.explanation: Do not back up or turn around on the highway. Continue to the next exit, then safely turn around.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left, drivers should:

options.text: Slow down gradually while checking the rearview mirror.
Watch for oncoming cars and pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Signal 3 to 5 seconds before turning. Check your rearview mirror and slow down gradually. Move into the left lane before the intersection. Let other cars and pedestrians pass, then turn when it is safe.

questions.question: You are driving at night with another vehicle approaching from the opposite direction. Your headlights should:

options.text: Be off. Use parking lights only.
Be on either high or low beam.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be on low beam.
questions.explanation: Do not use high beams when another car is coming toward you or when you are following another car at night. Use low beams to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: What can happen when you combine alcohol with another drug?

options.text: The effects of both may become stronger.
The effects of both may become weaker.
Only the alcohol effect may become weaker.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both may become stronger.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol with another drug can make both effects much stronger. For example, one drink mixed with a cold medicine could feel like you had several drinks.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when you are within 1,000 feet of an oncoming car or 500 feet of a car ahead of you. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: Many crashes are caused by:

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second distance behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast. Always drive within the speed limit and slow down when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give them room to pass safely.
questions.explanation: When a driver wants to pass you, slow down. This gives them enough room to pass quickly and safely.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass from your direction.

questions.question: A driver's ability can be impaired by:
questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires the driver to be in good health. Alcohol, drugs, and lack of sleep can all make driving unsafe.

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a T intersection is ahead.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between traffic lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass, even if it is dangerous.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes, but only if it is safe.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Use your horn to warn other drivers.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to blend with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: When driving on an interstate, what should you do?

options.text: Stop on the shoulder if you are tired.
Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or passing, signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency. Avoid changing lanes often. Do not use cruise control in heavy traffic or poor weather.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.correctAnswerText: Lower
questions.explanation: Lower your speed when turning. This lets you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when turning left, where should you look?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left shoulder.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, glance over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What do work zone signs mean?

options.text: You must stop and back up.
Drive faster to leave the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are not ideal.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and warn you that construction or maintenance is happening on or near the roadway. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: Colorado law requires headlights when visibility is less than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 1,000 feet.
questions.explanation: Colorado law requires you to use headlights between sunset and sunrise and whenever visibility is less than 1,000 feet. Driving in poor light conditions is more hazardous.

questions.question: What helps drivers save gasoline?

options.text: Leaving the car running in the driveway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down gradually.
questions.explanation: Every quick stop wastes fuel when you speed up again. Look ahead and slow down gradually or change lanes to avoid sudden braking. This saves gas.

questions.question: On a freeway, you missed your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make the turn quickly from your lane.
Keep driving until the next exit where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway. Continue to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: How should head restraints be positioned?

options.text: Touching the back of the head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Touching the back of the head.
questions.explanation: Adjust head restraints to touch the back of your head. This helps prevent injury during collisions, sudden stops, and sharp turns.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what headlights should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off fog and reflect into your eyes, making it harder to see.
